slides.heading: Classification of Infectious Diseases
slides.subtitle: How infections are grouped — by body involvement, behavior, severity, and host resistance.

slides.heading: WHO Goals
bullets: Prevention of disability and death from infection.

terms.definition: Confined to one specific area; localized signs.
Microorganisms spread and damage different parts of the body; generalized signs.
Caused by invasion and multiplication of a microorganism.
Spreads easily from one person to another.

slides.heading: By Severity / Duration
bullets: Acute — develops rapidly, lasts a short time (days–weeks): Measles, Mumps, Rubella, Varicella, Hepatitis A.
Chronic — develops slowly, milder but longer-lasting (months–lifelong): TB, leprosy, Herpes Simplex 1 & 2, Hepatitis B/C/D.
Hepatitis B, C, D treated with Interferon IM; Hepatitis D requires co-infection/superinfection with Hepatitis B.

terms.definition: Acute infection causing the initial illness.
Caused by an opportunistic pathogen after defenses are weakened.
Hospital/facility-based — develops during a stay or appears 48 hours after admission/discharge.
Procedure-based — a direct result of diagnostic, therapeutic or invasive procedures.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Classify by: body involvement, behavior in host, severity/duration, host resistance.
Endogenous = from patient; exogenous = from environment.
Nosocomial = facility-acquired (48 h rule); iatrogenic = procedure-caused.
Acute = MMRV/Hep A; chronic = TB, leprosy, HSV, Hep B/C/D.
